Alright, let me think through this year on my 14 mu...

I've been doing wheat-maize for as long as I can remember, like most folks around here. With 6 people in the family, we need both the grain for ourselves and some to sell. My oldest helps in the field during busy times, the younger ones are in school. My wife and I do most of the work, and I hire the combine for harvest — nobody around here does it by hand anymore.

**Wheat first.** I planted in early October last fall, the usual time. By now it should be greening up. I'll topdress urea around jointing in late March — extension station told us 15 kg N per mu is enough but I usually put a bit more, maybe 18, because last year my neighbor Old Wang got a better yield and I think he uses more. I already put about 30 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base before planting. For irrigation, I'll do the green-up watering, then jointing, then grain-fill if it doesn't rain — that's three times normally, but the well water costs money to pump so I watch the sky. If we get good spring rain I'll skip one. I'm hoping for around 480 kg/mu, which is what I got last year.

**Then maize, right after wheat in mid-June.** This is the tight part — the combine comes through, I have maybe 4-5 days to clear straw and plant. I do no-till direct seeding with a hired planter, costs me about 30 yuan/mu but saves three days of work. Hybrid seed from the agricultural supply shop, the Zhengdan variety most people use here. Base fertilizer goes down with the seed, then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage — total about 16 kg N/mu. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat in our area, usually one irrigation if July is dry. Last year I got around 500 kg/mu, I'll plan for similar.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once for both crops, that's standard. If I see armyworm or aphids on the maize I'll spray, but I don't pre-spray, that wastes money.
